title: Running Student
statementMd:
And again a misfortune fell on Poor Student. He is being late for an exam.

Having rushed to a bus stop that is in point $(0, 0)$, he got on a minibus and they drove along a straight line, parallel to axis $*OX*$, in the direction of increasing $*x*$.

Poor Student knows the following:

- during one run the minibus makes $*n*$ stops, the $*i*$-th stop is in point $(*x*_{*i*}, 0)$
- coordinates of all the stops are different
- the minibus drives at a constant speed, equal to $*v*_{*b*}$
- it can be assumed the passengers get on and off the minibus at a bus stop momentarily
- Student can get off the minibus only at a bus stop
- Student will have to get off the minibus at a terminal stop, if he does not get off earlier
- the University, where the exam will be held, is in point $(*x*_{*u*}, *y*_{*u*})$
- Student can run from a bus stop to the University at a constant speed $*v*_{*s*}$ as long as needed
- a distance between two points can be calculated according to the following formula: ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4e2bc133b4dc1a3376e33290ec54d4d1cea42685.png)
- Student is already on the minibus, so, he cannot get off at the first bus stop

Poor Student wants to get to the University as soon as possible. Help him to choose the bus stop, where he should get off. If such bus stops are multiple, choose the bus stop closest to the University.

## Input

The first line contains three integer numbers: $2 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$, $1 ≤ *v*_{*b*}, *v*_{*s*} ≤ 1000$. The second line contains $*n*$ non-negative integers in ascending order: coordinates $*x*_{*i*}$ of the bus stop with index $*i*$. It is guaranteed that $*x*_{1}$ equals to zero, and $*x*_{*n*} ≤ 10^{5}$. The third line contains the coordinates of the University, integers $*x*_{*u*}$ and $*y*_{*u*}$, not exceeding $10^{5}$ in absolute value.

## Output

In the only line output the answer to the problem — index of the optimum bus stop.

## Note

As you know, students are a special sort of people, and minibuses usually do not hurry. That's why you should not be surprised, if Student's speed is higher than the speed of the minibus.
statementZhMd:
又一次，不幸降临到了可怜的学生身上。他要赶不上考试了。

他急忙赶到了位于点 $(0, 0)$ 的公交车站，登上了一辆小巴士。小巴士沿着一条平行于坐标轴 *OX* 的直线，向 *x* 增大的方向行驶。

可怜的学生知道以下信息：

- 小巴士在一次行程中会停靠 *n* 个车站，第 *i* 个车站位于点 (*x*_{*i*}, 0)
- 所有车站的坐标各不相同
- 小巴士以恒定速度行驶，速度为 *v*_{*b*}
- 可以认为乘客在车站上下车的过程瞬间完成
- 学生只能在车站下车
- 如果学生没有提前下车，那么他必须在终点站下车
- 举行考试的大学位于点 (*x*_{*u*}, *y*_{*u*})
- 学生可以以恒定速度 *v*_{*s*} 从车站跑到大学，且奔跑时间不受限制
- 两点之间的距离可以根据以下公式计算：![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4e2bc133b4dc1a3376e33290ec54d4d1cea42685.png)
- 学生已经在小巴士上，因此不能在第一个车站下车

可怜的学生希望尽快到达大学。请帮助他选择应该下车的车站。如果有多个这样的车站，则选择距离大学最近的车站。

## 输入格式

第一行包含三个整数：$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$，$1 ≤ *v*_{*b*}, *v*_{*s*} ≤ 1000$。第二行包含 *n* 个按升序排列的非负整数：编号为 *i* 的车站的坐标 *x*_{*i*}。保证 *x*_{1} 等于零，且 *x*_{*n*} ≤ 10^{5}。第三行包含大学的坐标，即整数 *x*_{*u*} 和 *y*_{*u*}，它们的绝对值不超过 $10^{5}$。

## 输出格式

在唯一一行中输出问题的答案——最优车站的编号。

## 说明

众所周知，学生是一类特殊的人，而小巴士通常不会赶时间。因此，如果学生的速度高于小巴士的速度，也不必感到惊讶。
